answer.worked:
When $x=0$, $y=-5$.
$$\begin{align*}y&=(x^2+4x+4)-4-5\\y&=(x+2)^2-9\end{align*}$$
Axis $x=-2$; vertex $(-2,-9)$. At the $x$-intercepts:
$$\begin{align*}(x+2)^2&=9\\x+2&=\pm3\\x&=-5\text{ or }1\end{align*}$$
Sketch an upward-opening parabola through $(-5,0)$, $(1,0)$ and $(0,-5)$, symmetric about $x=-2$.

$$\begin{align*}y&=-(x^2-2x+2)\\y&=-[(x^2-2x+1)+2-1]\\y&=-(x-1)^2-1\end{align*}$$
